reader_operations.new:
Kim Anami calls the sexual current between encounters “the simmer”. Maybe she texts from work, “I can’t wait to touch you.” Maybe he tells her what he wants to do later. If we supposedly want each other but hardly ever flirt or let each other know it, that’s called taking each other for granted. Great sex probably isn't going to materialize out of nowhere at bedtime just based on the flirting you did 5 years ago.

It shouldn't become relationship homework, either: “Hey babe, Kim Anami told me to flirt with you more.”

reader_operations.old: “We’re together” ... what does that mean exactly? I might hear sex, exclusivity, living together, money, children, caregiving in those two words. She might mean, “We really like each other; let’s see what happens.” I actually like letting a relationship flow without naming every part. The problem is when we’re using the same words for two different futures.
